newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas contract to help offset price volatilit.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas contract to help offset price volatilit.

text.p: A natural gas futures contract on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) will help U.K. gas traders to offset risk in an increasingly volatile spot market, IPE Business Analyst Steve Esau said on Monday.
"(The U.K.) spot market is a little murky...The prices and indices based on reported deals have yet to find widespread acceptance," said Esau, who is responsible for the contract launch.
In the U.S., the NYMEX natural gas futures contract is the key risk management tool in a highly volatile market, he told a conference.
"A significant amount of risk taken by the OTC (over the counter) risk providers is ultimately offset against the NYMEX natgas contract."
Gas prices in the U.K. are even more volatile than the U.S., said Esau.
"U.K. gas prices are subject to a more volatile demand profile and less storage capacity," he said.

Fuelled by the introduction of daily balancing, volumes traded on the U.K. spot market have increased sharply in recent months. On some days trade has exceeded 100 million therms, or some 30 million therms more than daily U.K. consumption.
Following the U.S. example, the IPE futures contract would offer the spot market a transparent benchmark pricing system, Esau said.
"Most natural gas transactions (in the U.S.) are priced through formulae that establish some sort of differential to the NYMEX contract."
The IPE hopes to launch a contract at both the Bacton beach terminal and the National Balancing Point (NBP) within the Transco system.
"It is our view that the NBP will become the focus of balancing or operational-type trading, and Bacton for futures-style trading which may not result in physical delivery," said Esau.
The NBP will trade three months ahead and the Bacton contract 12 months ahead.
"Contract development is complete for both but we have been hampered by third parties all down the line," Esau said.
"We have a good deal more confidence in the NBP contract...approval from the regulator of the Network Code modification is expected next week."
But even when all approvals are in place, the industry will be given six to eight weeks' notice.

The launch of the Bacton contract is still dogged by the failure of the Claims Validation Agent (CVA) to come up with an effective mechanism for the verification of physical deliveries of gas at the beach.
"We won't speculate about a launch date (for either contract). When we announce it we will be 100 percent certain," said Esau.
